title: Angels from the Realms of Glory
description: The UK version: James Montgomery's Christmas hymn to the French carol tune Iris ("Les anges dans nos campagnes"), the tune UK churches sing these words to, with its refrain "Gloria in excelsis Deo", in S. S. Greatheed's four parts from R. R. Chope's Carols for Use in Church (1875), arranged for 2 to 4 singers. Chope printed Greatheed's harmony with other words, so this pairing of Montgomery's words with it is our own, his longer lines fitted to the verse by splitting one note in two. Verses 1 to 3, the angels, the shepherds and the sages, in F, each followed by the Gloria, whose long run on "Glo-" steps down, bar after bar.

credits.words: James Montgomery (The Christian Psalmist, 1825); refrain "Gloria in excelsis Deo" as Chope prints it with the tune
credits.tune: "Iris" ("Les anges dans nos campagnes"), traditional French
credits.arrangement: S. S. Greatheed's four parts (R. R. Chope, Carols for Use in Church, 1875), adapted by Stackapella

licence.words: public domain: James Montgomery died 1854 (hymnary.org/person/Montgomery_James: "1771-1854"; Wikipedia, James Montgomery (poet): died 30 April 1854, Sheffield); verses 1 to 3 of the five of his No. 487, "Good tidings of great joy to all people", as The Christian Psalmist (Glasgow, 1825) prints them, his punctuation and spellings kept; his refrain "Come and worship, / Worship Christ the new-born King" is not sung: each verse is followed by the Latin refrain "Gloria in excelsis Deo", sung twice, as Chope prints it under the tune
licence.tune: public domain: the traditional French carol tune of "Les anges dans nos campagnes", known in British hymn books as "Iris", given in Chope's index (p. xxxvi) as "Traditional"; no maker
licence.arrangement: Greatheed's own four parts, signed in Chope's index (p. xxxvi) "Traditional, arranged by the Rev. S. S. Greatheed" and marked as new to the book (Greatheed died 1887; Chope died 1928; the book's music editor Herbert Stephen Irons died 1905; public domain), in his key (F) and his chords, with Montgomery's words underlaid in place of Chope's (our own pairing: Chope prints the tune to "When the crimson sun had set") and these changes (pitches as written here, in F). Re-underlay, with rhythm splits only and no new pitches: Greatheed's verse is four bars sung twice to a 7.7.7.7 couplet, and Montgomery's 8.7.8.7 verse is sung to it the same way, lines 1 and 2 then lines 3 and 4; in the 8-syllable lines (1 and 3 of every verse) the minim that ends the second bar is sung as two crotchets on the same note in every part (the tune's A4, A4), for the extra weak syllable of "glo-ry", "sto-ry", "a-bid-ing", "re-sid-ing", "con-tem-pla-tions" and "of na-tions"; the 7-syllable lines take one syllable a note as printed. For one note a syllable, the tenor and bass, which change chord on the second crotchet of that bar while the tune holds its dotted crotchet, move with the tune's quaver instead (tenor D4 throughout, bass B-flat 2 for the dotted crotchet, then D3 on "of", "tion's", "a-", "re-", "tem-", "of"); in the fourth bar the bass sings C3 for the tune's dotted crotchet ("all", "si-", "flocks", "in-", "beam", "na-"; his C4, above the beginner range, then C3 on the second crotchet) and C3 again on the quaver, and F3 on the third bar's last crotchet ("o'er", "Mes-", "your", "the", "sions", "his"; his A3), so it falls a fourth into the cadence. In the chorus every lower part sings "Glo-" through the Gloria run, one note a chord, as printed (Greatheed moves them in crotchets); the tenor sings A3 on each Gloria's fourth crotchet (his D4), so the D chord over F sharp has its fifth and the tenor's line moves by step down to G3 (the tune's passing B-flat 4 quaver sounds against it); on the first "De-o," the tenor holds A3 through "De-" (his F3, then quavers A3 and C4) and the bass holds C3 (his C3, then quavers F3 and A3) and sings C3 on "o," (his C4, above the beginner range). In the last line the alto sings D4 on "sis" (his G4), C4 on "De-" and B-flat 3 under the tune's G4 (his G4, F4, F4, E4), and A3 on "o." (his F4, in unison with the tune), and the tenor A3 and F3 on "cel-sis" (his C4 and D4), F3 on "De-", E3 under the G4 (his C4, then B-flat 3) and F3 on "o." (his A3): the alto takes his tenor's falling C, B-flat, A in sixths under the tune and the tenor his alto's line an octave lower, so the duet and trio end with the third; the bass ends on F3 (he prints F3 and F2 together). Breaths written in for beginners: "earth" and "birth" give up a beat of their minim, as do "a" of each "Glo-ri-a" and the first "o,", and a bar's rest follows each verse's last "o.". Accepted exceptions: the tune's low C4 on "ri-a" (twice each chorus), under the beginner soprano's D4, as printed, the key kept as every other part sits in range; the alto a third above the tune there (E4 over C4, two and a half beats), Greatheed's own, approached by step; the duet's bare fifth C5 over F4 on the dotted crotchet of the 8-syllable lines ("realms", "a-" of "creation's", "field", "now", "con-", "sire"), where the tune's C5 leans on Greatheed's B-flat chord and a third, D4, would sound a seventh against it; his unison F4 on "earth" and "birth", where his alto's E rises to the tune's F as a two-part close (the trio has no third there; the tenor has it in four parts), and on the second "in" for one crotchet, approached by step; the alto's C4 an octave under the tune's C5 for a quaver, under the run in each Gloria's second bar; the trio without a third on the B-flat chord in each Gloria's third bar and the F chord on its second crotchet in the second Gloria (the tenor has it); the lower parts' notes on "Glo-" (one a chord, as in our Angels We Have Heard on High); Greatheed's tenor rising G3, C4, D4 through each Gloria's second and third bars; the alto's sixth from A3 up to F4 across the bar's rest between verses; and the last chord without a fifth, as Greatheed prints it. The bass sings Greatheed's A3 before each verse line's cadence and F3 on the dotted note (his C4), so that chord has its third and the cadence runs F, C7, F; and it holds G3 for two beats in each Gloria where Greatheed passes through F3. The alto moves with the tune's dotted rhythm in the verse's fourth bar (his F4, E4 as two crotchets). Also without a third: the trio's B-flat chord on the verse's dotted note (B-flat 2, F4, C5), and the duet and trio's C7 on the last "De-" (G4 over B-flat 3, the C in the bass).
licence.source: R. R. Chope, Carols for Use in Church during Christmas and Epiphany, the music edited by Herbert Stephen Irons, with an introduction by S. Baring-Gould (London: Metzler & Co. and Novello, Ewer, & Co., 1875; the index signed "Wilton House, Hereford Square, S.W., 1875"), Carol 68, "When the crimson sun had set" (words by the Rev. George Peirce Grantham, not sung here), p. 139, a four-bar Verse with repeat marks and a thirteen-bar Chorus, "Gloria in excelsis Deo" twice, in four parts on two staves in F major (one flat), C time, in its printed key here (F); read from the Princeton Theological Seminary Library copy at archive.org/details/carolnch00chop/page/n178 (the index, p. xxxvi, at n39; the title page at n4). Words from James Montgomery, The Christian Psalmist (Glasgow, 1825), No. 487, pp. 389 and 390, archive.org/details/christianpsalmis00montiala/page/n406 and n407. The wording is the same as our US version's (Hutchins, 1894); the punctuation and capitals here are Montgomery's: "Angels, from", "Shepherds, in", "Ye who sang", "earth,", "birth;", "night,", "infant-light;", "contemplations,", "afar;", "nations;" and "his natal star;" (Hutchins: "Angels from", "Shepherds in", "Ye, who sang", "earth;", "birth:", "night;", "infant-light:", "contemplations;", "afar:", "nations,", "His natal star:")
